title: VTA Memory List — payload
description: Enumerate the memory items in a context. Two modes, distinguished by whether `sinceVersion` is supplied. Without it this is a SNAPSHOT of live items, optionally narrowed by `prefix`. With it this is a CHANGE FEED: every item in the context whose version exceeds the watermark, tombstones included, which is what lets an agent's local cache on another device converge. Pagination is opaque-cursor based.

contextId.description: The VTA context to enumerate; the isolation boundary.

prefix.description: Restrict to items whose `key` begins with this byte prefix, compared over the UTF-8 encoding. Lets an agent recall one family of items — `contact/`, `preference/` — without dragging the whole context through the response.

sinceVersion.description: Watermark. Selects change-feed mode: only items whose `version` is strictly greater are returned, tombstones included. Supply the `highWatermark` from the previous sync, or 0 for a first full pull in change-feed form.

includeValues.description: When true, each returned item carries its `value`. Defaults to TRUE — unlike vta/app-state/list — because recalling the text is what an agent lists memory for, and 0.1 always returned values. Set it false for the metadata view (key, version, timestamps, `valueBytes`), which makes a scan of a large context cheap.

includeDeleted.description: Snapshot mode only: when true, tombstones still inside the retention window are returned alongside live items. Defaults to false. In change-feed mode tombstones are always returned and this member MUST NOT be set to false — a change feed that omits deletions cannot converge.

cursor.description: An opaque continuation token from a previous response's `nextCursor`; a responder MUST NOT accept a cursor it did not issue. Consumers MUST treat it as opaque: never construct, decode, mutate, or infer meaning from one.

limit.description: The most items to return; the responder chooses a default and MAY return fewer, which is likely when `includeValues` is in effect and the values are large.

items.description: Matching items in ascending key order in snapshot mode, and ascending version order in change-feed mode — the latter so that a consumer applying them in order reaches the same state as the maintainer. May be empty.

nextCursor.description: Opaque continuation token for the next page, sent back as the request's `cursor`. Present when more matching items exist beyond this page; absent on the last page.

highWatermark.description: The context's current counter value; 0 for a context that has never been written. This is what a consumer stores as its next `sinceVersion` — NOT the maximum version among `items`, which is wrong whenever a `prefix` filtered a later change out, and undefined when the page is empty. A paginating consumer MUST NOT advance its stored watermark until it has drained the final page — the one with no `nextCursor` — because the pages of one feed share this value and adopting it early would skip the items still to come.

tombstoneRetentionSeconds.description: How long this maintainer retains tombstones before reaping them. Advisory, so a consumer can schedule its syncs to stay inside the window rather than discovering it has fallen out of it via vta/memory/list:watermarkTooOld.
